events.title: Extreme heat warnings issued for parts of southern California
events.summary:
Temperatures in US state forecast to hit high 30s celsius this week, while regions in Indonesia grapple with wildfires

The National Weather Service in the US has issued extreme heat warnings for parts of southern California, including Los Angeles, until Thursday, as temperatures are expected to hit the high 30s celsius. Burbank, a suburb north of Los Angeles, recorded 39C on Saturday, a few degrees shy of the October record for the region set in 1987. A persistent area of high pressure will remain in place this week, leading to further hazardous hot weather and increased fire risk.

Parts of Indonesia are in the midst of an extreme wildfire season, which has peaked over the past month. Western Kalimantan (Borneo) and southern Sumatra have been particularly badly affected. The lack of rainfall has dried the usually water-logged tropical soils, meaning that fires have been able to spread quickly, above and below the surface. Indonesia’s soils are also extremely rich in peat, meaning that the smoke produced from the fires contain higher levels of toxic gases such as sulphur dioxide and carbon monoxide. Cities in surrounding areas and as far as Malaysia and Singapore have experienced reduced air quality in recent weeks as a result. Drought and wildfires are more common in this part of the world during El Niño events owing to suppressed thunderstorm activity.

The weather pattern, known as a Dana, occurs most often in autumn.

Models show more than 100mm of rain could fall across the region on Friday, with 200-300mm possible in some areas. Cities including Valencia and Castelló de la Plana, are most at risk. Valencia has experienced several damaging floods in recent years. Catalonia has now put three towns under lockdown and Valencia has shut schools for nearly half a million children.

Students are furious at what they say is a chronic lack of funding for state schools, with that anger exacerbated by accusations that state resources are unfairly distributed, with richer and whiter postcodes historically receiving the lion's share of funds.

events.title: Up to 500 French schools to be closed Monday as protests continue
events.summary: Up to 500 French high ⁠schools will begin a second week of total or partial closures on Monday as protests over dilapidated schools and classrooms, overcrowding and teacher shortages precede a nationwide day of demonstrations on Tuesday. events.title: U.S. Marine arrested on suspicion of killing Japanese woman in Okinawa
events.summary: Japan’s Defense Ministry said it was “deeply outraged by the extremely brutal and heinous crime committed by a U.S. Marine.”

events.title: Flydubai pilot attacked captain with cockpit’s crash ax in attempted terrorist act, UAE official says
events.summary: TEL AVIV — A Flydubai pilot attacked his flight captain using a crash ax and tried to take control of the aircraft’s controls in an attempted terrorist attack, an official with the United Arab Emirates said Saturday.

events.title: Two Iranian nationals charged over alleged terrorism plot targeting Jewish community in England
events.summary: British police said Friday that they had charged two Iranian nationals accused of plotting a terrorist attack against the Jewish community in Manchester on the eve of Yom Kippur, the holiest day in the Jewish calendar.

events.title: Screaming, panicking, blood: Passengers detail horrifying Israel-bound flight
events.summary: It was too early to say why a pilot stabbed another on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

events.title: What we know about the cockpit stabbing on Israel-bound flight
events.summary: What we know about the potential midair disaster aboard the Flydubai flight when a pilot attacked his colleague causing the plane to plunge thousands of feet.

events.title: Britain believes Iran was involved in incident near air base used by U.S., prime minister says
events.summary: Five men were arrested on suspicion of terrorist offenses in the incident outside RAF Fairford. Iran had denied any involvement.

events.title: What we know about the pilot hailed as a hero for averting crash of Israel-bound plane
events.summary: He is being hailed around the world as a hero for helping stop a passenger plane bound for Israel from plunging into the ground, despite his own severe injuries.

events.title: Pilot stabbed his co-pilot in apparent attempt to crash Israel-bound plane, Netanyahu says
events.summary: On-duty crewmembers were able to divert and land the aircraft safely at Tabuk Airport, the airline said.

events.title: British police find no explosives in vehicles of men detained near base used by U.S.
events.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the incident near RAF Fairford, which facilitates strikes on Iran, “clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor,” an allegation British officials haven’t confirmed.

events.title: Settlers clash with Israeli forces to block Palestinian family’s return home
events.summary: It is the second time the Tubassi family has suffered at the hands of Jewish settlers in just over a month. On Aug. 28, masked settlers attacked and injured them and an NBC News crew that was interviewing them.

events.title: A search for their loved ones’ remains, three months after Venezuela earthquakes
events.summary: Sleeping in tents in front of collapsed buildings and removing rubble with bare hands, family members and volunteers search the ruins with at least 1,500 people missing.

events.title: Terrorism suspects arrested near British air base used by U.S. are released on bail
events.summary: The five British nationals were detained after a massive security operation near a base the U.S. uses to facilitate strikes on Iran.
